title: two flags on one cart

opening.dialogue: A life is a sending: the camp gate sends its men out at six and takes their wages back at seven. Kwang stands at the hoarding with a phone mount clamped to a fence wire, a woman running at five percent, photographing a mortar that is not hers.
Lek. Hold the mount steady — the light here is the only honest thing on this soi. My kitchen flew two flags and neither of them was this one.
Behind her, Pa Yong's cart sits under its tarp. The new item on the page has sold out three times. Pa Yong has not spoken to her daughter since the order came in.

turns.speaker: char_kwang
stage_directions: She raises her palm flat at the fence line, stopping a camp worker from walking through her shot.
turns.dialogue: Stop right there — one more step and the mortar's shadow lands on your boot. The frame is the whole argument.

turns.speaker: char_kwang
stage_directions: She keeps her hand up, the phone mount still level, and talks over the worker's apology.
turns.dialogue: I'm not finished. The caption has to say 'her mother's mortar' and mean it, or the whole page reads like a menu.

turns.speaker: char_kwang
stage_directions: She turns the mount toward Ko Naing and waves her free hand flat, apologetic, at the tarp.
turns.dialogue: He can't speak Thai and I can't speak Mon, so we nod at each other like two clocks in different time zones. Ask him if the tarp can move.

turns.speaker: char_kwang
stage_directions: A vendor's boy holds out a tea glass; she pushes it gently back with two fingers.
turns.dialogue: I don't want it. If I hold a glass in the shot, the brand reads as a drink, and the mortar disappears.

turns.speaker: char_kwang
stage_directions: She lowers the mount and turns fully toward Lek, the charger bank in her other hand already unplugged.
turns.dialogue: Oh, it's you — good. The tower's laundry room is overpriced and my phone is at five percent. Hold this bank and keep the light on the mortar.

turns.speaker: char_kwang
stage_directions: She hooks her pinky around the change-machine key and holds it out toward Lek.
turns.dialogue: Promise me you won't tell Pa Yong I was here on a Sunday. She'll say I came to photograph her mortar for the tower's brochure.

turns.speaker: char_kwang
stage_directions: She unfolds a printed map of the soi against the hoarding and taps the camp gate with the key.
turns.dialogue: Tell me how to get to the last rai from here without walking past the cart. I need the farmland in the background, not the tarp.

turns.speaker: char_kwang
stage_directions: She scrolls the shot list on the mount's screen and taps the last line with the key.
turns.dialogue: Mortar, tarp, farmland, daughter's hands. That's all, isn't it? Then I can send it before the battery dies.

kwang_turn_1.speaker: char_kwang
kwang_turn_1.line: The worker steps back. The mortar's shadow falls clean across the tarp, and Kwang exhales like she has won something small.

kwang_turn_2.speaker: char_kwang
kwang_turn_2.line: She keeps talking to the fence wire. The tea glass sits untouched on the cart's edge, sweating in the heat.

kwang_turn_3.speaker: char_kwang
kwang_turn_3.line: Ko Naing nods once and drags the tarp a meter left. The mortar comes into the frame, and Kwang's thumb moves fast.
kwang_turn_3.bubble: The tarp has moved; the mortar is visible

kwang_turn_4.speaker: char_kwang
kwang_turn_4.line: The boy takes the glass back. Kwang's shot stays clean, and the vendor's boy watches her from the shade with no expression at all.

kwang_turn_5.speaker: char_kwang
kwang_turn_5.line: The charger bank clicks into her phone. The screen brightens, and the mortar on it looks older than the cart it sits on.

kwang_turn_6.speaker: char_kwang
kwang_turn_6.line: She presses the key into Lek's palm and closes his fingers over it. 'The change machine at the laundromat. If Pa Yong asks, you never saw me.'

kwang_turn_7.speaker: char_kwang
kwang_turn_7.line: She traces the route with the key and folds the map. 'Past the wat, then the last rai. I'll send the shot from the tower tonight.'

kwang_turn_8.speaker: char_kwang
kwang_turn_8.line: She reads the list twice, deletes the line about the daughter's hands, and says nothing about why.

finale.dialogue: She unclamps the mount and walks toward the tower, the phone at five percent and climbing. 'Tell Pa Yong the mortar photographs well. That's all I'll say.'
The tarp goes back over the cart. The camp gate sends its men out at six, and the mortar waits under the canvas for whatever the page decides it is.

obj_stamp_keys.name: the stamp-drawer keys
obj_stamp_keys.description: Two brass keys on a wire ring, worn smooth at the bow, one of them opening the drawer where Khun Sanga keeps the date stamps and the other opening nothing anyone remembers.

obj_biscuit_tin.name: the biscuit tin of ledgers
obj_biscuit_tin.description: A square biscuit tin, lid dented at one corner, holding three vendors' books in rubber bands and a smell of old paper and lemongrass.

obj_score_report.name: the laminated score report
obj_score_report.description: A laminated exam result, folded twice, the score circled in red pen: three points short, twice over, the lamination gone cloudy at the crease.

obj_charger_bank.name: the charger bank
obj_charger_bank.description: A palm-sized power bank, scuffed gray, with a strip of green tape on one side and a charge light that goes from red to white.

obj_green_jacket.name: the green rider jacket
obj_green_jacket.description: A green delivery jacket hung on the hoarding wire, reflective stripe peeling at the shoulder, the name of no company on the back.

obj_gimbal.name: the funeral gimbal
obj_gimbal.description: A handheld gimbal with a phone clamp, one arm taped where it was dropped at a funeral livestream, the motor still whining softly when switched on.

obj_change_key.name: the change-machine key
obj_change_key.description: A flat key on a plastic tag, the tag written in marker with a number that has faded to a suggestion, the key to the change machine at Saduek Sak 24.

obj_tea_glass.name: the tea-stall glass
obj_tea_glass.description: A small glass, thick-walled, with a hairline crack near the base and a ring of tea stain that never quite washes out.

obj_phone_mount.name: the phone mount
obj_phone_mount.description: A clamp mount with a ball joint, the rubber pad on the jaw worn through to the metal, clamped to a fence wire and holding a phone at eye level.

outcomeRules.speaker: char_kwang
outcomeRules.line: She takes the keys and turns them in the light. 'The copy shop's stamps. If I photograph the mortar on your counter, it reads as a document, not a menu.'
outcomeRules.bubble: Kwang wants the mortar photographed on the copy-shop counter

outcomeRules.speaker: char_kwang
outcomeRules.line: She opens the tin and reads a vendor's page upside down. 'Three ledgers and a mortar. Put the tin in the shot and the cart becomes a business, not a trend.'
outcomeRules.bubble: Kwang has the shot she came for

char_kwang: She turns the {item} over once and hands it back. 'Not that. The light's moving and the battery's dying.'
She sets the {item} on the hoarding ledge between them. 'The mortar first. Everything else is a caption.'
She taps the phone mount with the {item}. 'The copy shop's stamps. If the mortar sits on your counter, the page reads as a document. That's the shot.'
narrator: The {item} goes back into the heat with nothing settled. Kwang's phone ticks down a percent.
Nothing comes of the {item} yet. The camp gate opens and closes; the tarp does not move.
Kwang's gaze flicks from the {item} to the copy shop's direction and back — a counter mapped, a stamp implied.
